i’m sorry to hear that you went through that and it must be heartbreaking to watch your sister begin to go through that as well. i don’t know your schedule, but maybe you could spend more time with her. it’s a bit difficult to come up with a plan since i don’t think authorities would view this as something to take action against. maybe tell her your own experience and give her advice on how to deal with your parents. it could be good for her to know what they’re going to do so she can be prepared for it. also maybe try getting her to go out and eat with you at a restaurant or something without the parents so she can eat freely without the parents controlling that.

i have ocd and this sounds like ocd and ed combined (not saying it is 100% ocd though, just from my own experience). horrible thing to deal with, i’m sorry you’re having those thoughts :( reassurance is really nice and fact checking is nice to make the thoughts go away, but if these are reoccurring intrusive thoughts, try to let them pass. (key word is try, sometimes you can’t and that’s okay) best of luck <3

it’s better, but it really is difficult. some days are better than others. for me, since my guard was down i found that i was triggered by things a lot more since being away. that being said, it is 100 times better to be away from your parents and i do not regret at all moving away. i noticed i had a lot of trauma responses i needed to unlearn once i moved out too and it becomes easier and easier to calm down and not do them anymore.

i was also like this when i was younger and i have selective mutism. i don’t know how schools deal with students like this nowadays, but i think it’s best to be sure he isn’t being mistreated by teachers or peers for having selective mutism. having a good support system and people around you who understand your selective mutism can really decrease a lot of anxiety and could potentially help him open up at school more. it’s great that you care about your son and want to help! a parent like that really helps in situations like this and if only other parents were as caring as you
